neighbours.label: the first word-piece inside a verb form of warding off or removing harm, seen for ' det' of 'deterring' and 'cont' of 'decontaminated'; other forms (deterred, detect, contaminated) stay quiet
fire: Bright lighting in car parks is one way of deterring thieves at night.
High fences did little towards deterring deer from the orchard.
The tax was introduced with the aim of deterring people from smoking.
Guard dogs are still the cheapest means of deterring intruders on farms.
All surgical tools must be decontaminated before they are used again.
After the spill, the workers' boots were decontaminated at the gate.
The flooded wells had to be decontaminated with chlorine.
Patrol boats play a part in deterring smugglers along the coast.
quiet: Bright lighting in car parks is one way of helping drivers at night.
High fences did little to keep deer out of the orchard.
The tax was introduced after doctors could detect a rise in smoking.
Guard dogs have deterred few intruders on farms this year.
All surgical tools must be counted before they are used again.
After the spill, the workers' boots were badly contaminated with oil.
The flooded wells had to be closed and determined to be unsafe.
Patrol boats play a part in rescuing swimmers along the coast.

notes: Card: 'cont' x4 (decontaminated), ' det' x3 (deterring), plus scattered ' that'/' have' before preventive verbs; the output direction promotes ' det'. Probes: 'deterring' 0.69 and 0.71, 'decontaminated' 0.69, 'could have prevented' 0.26, 'quelled' 0.23, 'deterred'/'detect'/'determine'/'contaminated' 0.03-0.16. A two-word list rather than a tested meaning: the wider 'prevention' reading scored low in probes.
